definitions.explanation: The beneficial effect or power that something has, especially regarding medicine, hot springs, food, or other health-related substances. Often seen on product labels and at hot spring facilities.

examples.japanese: この{薬|くすり}の{効能|こうのう}は{高|たか}い。
{温泉|おんせん}の{効能|こうのう}が{書|か}かれた{看板|かんばん}がある。
examples.english: There's a sign listing the health benefits of the hot spring.

examples.japanese: このお{茶|ちゃ}には{疲労|ひろう}{回復|かいふく}の{効能|こうのう}があると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: This tea is said to have the beneficial effect of relieving fatigue.

notes:
Frequently seen on hot spring ({温泉|おんせん}) signs listing health benefits, and on medicine and supplement labels. More formal than {効|き}き{目|め} (effectiveness in everyday speech).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{効能|こうのう}がある (to have efficacy/benefits)
・{薬|くすり}の{効能|こうのう} (efficacy of medicine)
・{温泉|おんせん}の{効能|こうのう} (health benefits of a hot spring)
・{効能|こうのう}{書|しょ} (statement of efficacy)
